title.narrative: Access Governance & Reform for the Electricity and Water Sectors Project

description.narrative: Operation Abstract: Summary Description of Proposed Project (Restructured as part of Level 2 Restructuring package, 2026)The project aims to significantly scale up access to electricity and water services in priority areas of the DRC while improving utility governance and performance and strengthening public institution capacity. It targets provinces prioritized in the Country Partnership Framework 2022-2026. Following the Level 2 deep restructuring agreed at the February 2026 Mid-Term Review, the project's scope has been reduced by approximately 50%, refocusing exclusively on activities that directly contribute to the PDO and are realistically achievable before the September 30, 2029 closing date. As a result, a partial cancellation of US$100 million of IDA financing has been processed, reducing the total IDA envelope from US$600 million to US$500 million. Project components 1 and 2 will address market failures (e.g., tariffs, regulations), support SNEL reform and REGIDESO transformation, and strengthen governance, regulatory and implementing capacity of national institutions. Component 3 will use grants to leverage private sector investments through the Mwinda Fund — the primary vehicle for expanding electricity access — following the cancellation of the SMG sub-program for Kananga and Mbuji-Mayi. The combined IDA, GCF, and AFD financing is expected to mobilize private capital through Results-Based Grants and risk mitigation instruments in coordination with IFC and MIGA. In selected cities serviced by SNEL and REGIDESO, component 4 will finance network rehabilitation and expansion to increase and/or improve electricity and drinking water services.The project will leverage synergies between the energy and water sectors to provide a package of electricity and water services to households, productive and community users (schools, health centers) in targeted cities. In Kinshasa, the distribution network will be rehabilitated and expanded, with procurement for two lots well advanced and delivery of 110,000 prepaid meters expected by April 2026, to enhance the quality of and increase access to electricity for households and small and medium enterprises. In Kananga, the project will construct a new water treatment plant (US$100 million), rehabilitate the existing Kanyuka treatment plant (US$25 million), and expand distribution networks (US$35 million), with contract signatures expected by May 2026. The Mwinda Fund (Subcomponent 3.2) — now significantly scaled up through the reallocation of funds from cancelled SMG activities — will provide Results-Based Grants to private electricity operators expanding connections through mini-grids, Solar Home Systems, and valorization of surplus production across targeted areas. In Gbadolite, subject to the resolution of critical logistical constraints for the transport of heavy equipment, the rehabilitation of one generation unit at the Mobayi-Mbongo Hydropower plant will be completed and the operation and management of the associated distribution network improved. In Kabinda, AFD co-financing (EUR 41 million, ring-fenced exclusively for this purpose) will support the electrification through a minigrid concession under the SMG approach. Activities in Goma, Bukavu, Beni, and Butembo have been cancelled due to security constraints and the related budget transferred to remaining priority activities. Inga 3 support activities are being transferred to the newly established Inga 3 Development Project (PDI3, P512835). All investments and technical assistance will be climate-proofed and include specific measures to mitigate and/or adapt to climate change.The project comprises four components and a CERC component.Component 1: Power and Water Utility Governance and Performance (IDA: revised budget). This component supports the GoDRC's plan to advance reforms of SNEL and REGIDESO while improving performance, through regular technical assistance replacing the original Performance Based Conditions (PBCs) which were unrealistic. In the electricity sector, advancing SNEL reform involves supporting restructuring option studies — including debt restructuring (Ernst & Young), legal classification of assets, and development of a restructuring roadmap by Tetratech — pending a government decision on the final restructuring option. In the water sector, REGIDESO's transformation strategy focuses on giving greater autonomy to regional directorates while establishing accountability through internal performance contracts, alongside digitalization and reduction of non-revenue water. Sub-component 1.3 has been renamed "REGIDESO Transformation and Performance Improvement" to reflect this revised strategy.Component 2: Institutional Strengthening and Development Support (IDA and GCF grant). This component bolsters the capacities of key public institutions at the national level. Sub-component 2.1 activities supporting provincial governments have been cancelled due to security constraints in eastern DRC. The project will continue to support the construction and equipping of a dedicated building to house sector agencies (ARE, ANSER, UCM, OCE) alongside the MRHE, with the scope and cost optimized following the MTR. Sub-component 2.3 has been refocused on mature planning activities directly contributing to the PDO, including priority hydropower and transmission investment studies, the national and rural electrification master plans, and hydropower site mapping, while preliminary planning studies have been channeled to the DRC Investment Facilitation Project under preparation.Component 3: Private Sector-based Access Expansion (IDA and GCF grant, co-financed by AFD). Following the formal cancellation of the SMG sub-program for Kananga and Mbuji-Mayi — due to the Government's failure to provide the required ministerial decrees for distribution concession perimeters and to submit convincing technical and operational options — Sub-component 3.1 is limited to the Kabinda minigrid concession, supported exclusively through AFD co-financing (EUR 41 million). Sub-component 3.2, the Mwinda Fund, has been significantly scaled up through the reallocation of funds from cancelled SMG activities, and will serve as the primary instrument for expanding electricity access through Results-Based Grants linked to verified and functioning connections across eligible technologies and target areas, in support of the Government's energy access priorities under the National Energy Compact. Sub-component 3.3 (support to private water operators) has been eliminated.Component 4: Public Sector-based Access Expansion with Private Sector Involvement (IDA: revised budget). The component finances the rehabilitation and expansion of power and water infrastructure in selected cities managed by SNEL and REGIDESO. In the electricity sector (Sub-component 4.1), procurement for the Mobayi hydropower plant rehabilitation and Kinshasa network densification is underway, though activities in Gbadolite and Mobayi remain subject to the resolution of logistical constraints by March 15, 2026. In the water sector (Sub-component 4.2), investments are solely focused on Kananga following the cancellation of activities in Goma, Bukavu, Beni, and Butembo due to security constraints. The sub-component is also expanded to include digital transformation support for REGIDESO. IDA funds will also cover approximately US$10 million for resettlement compensation (PAPs) under Sub-components 4.1 and 4.2. Sub-component 4.3 maintains its allocation for training and human capital development, including vocational training for 500 youth through INPP and Don Bosco partnerships.Component 5: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC). This CERC with zero allocation may be used to contribute to an emergency response through the timely implementation of activities in response to an eligible national emergency. A CERC is included in accordance with Investment Project Financing (IPF) Policy, paragraphs 12 and 13, for Situ

The objectives of the Project are to (i) expand access to renewable-based electricity and drinking water services in selected urban and peri-urban areas of the Democratic Republic of Congo, (ii) improve the commercial performance of the public electricity and water utilities, and (iii) strengthen the capacity of selected provincial and national institutions in the electricity and water sector.

title.narrative: Share of new positions/jobs within electricity and water entities that are taken by women (public and private)

This reflects early but promising momentum toward increasing women's participation in technical roles within the sector.
